expectations.tolerance_rationale: stats::varimax and GPArotation::GPForth both stop at a relative criterion of 1e-05; two converged implementations differ by a small multiple of that. tol = 10 * eps = 0.0001. Measured stats vs GPA on this input: 2.2e-05 normalized, 7.4e-06 un-normalized; 4.9e-05 on an 8x2 example. The normalization effect on this input is 1.38e-03, fourteen times the tolerance, so the two expectations cannot be confused by any converged implementation.

DeadNormalizeArgument.description: psych::Promax(x, m, normalize, pro.m, Tmat, ...) declares `normalize` as a formal argument and documents it as 'parameter passed to optimization routine', but the identifier does not occur in the function body. Because it is a named formal it is captured and never reaches `...`, so it cannot be forwarded to GPArotation::Varimax by that route either. Measured on psych 2.6.5: Promax(L, normalize=TRUE) and Promax(L, normalize=FALSE) differ by exactly 0.0; GPArotation::Varimax under the same two values differs by 1.38e-02. Fix is one token: `GPArotation::Varimax(x, Tmat = Tmat, normalize = normalize, ...)`. Verified to leave the shipped default bit-identical and to recover the pre-2.6.5 result within 4.9e-05.
DeadNormalizeArgument.name: DeadNormalizeArgument

SilentDefaultFlip.description: psych <= 2.6.3 computed the varimax stage with stats::varimax, whose default is normalize=TRUE. psych 2.6.5 computes it with GPArotation::Varimax behind a hardcoded `GPA <- TRUE`, whose default is normalize=FALSE. The user-visible argument did nothing in either version, so the effective behaviour changed from always-normalize to never-normalize with no NEWS entry and no way to request the old result. Measured: 1.38e-03 on this vector's input; up to 0.94 after optimal column alignment on ill-conditioned 8-variable matrices, where five of sixteen loadings change sign. The maintainer's first hypothesis, the new n.rotations multi-start option, moves fa(rotate='Promax') by 1.5e-06 to 5.5e-06 and does not reach Promax() at all.
SilentDefaultFlip.name: SilentDefaultFlip

authority.basis: Hendrickson & White 1964 sec. 2 for the two-step definition; Kaiser 1958 sec. 5 for normal varimax; R stats::promax and stats::varimax source for the reference algorithm. Measured on psych 2.6.5: Promax(normalize=TRUE) equals Promax(normalize=FALSE) to 0.0 and equals the un-normalized expectation to 0.0; the 2.6.3 code path equals the normalized expectation within 2.2e-05.
authority.claims: Under the declared conventions, these are the Promax loadings after column canonicalization. The two expectations differ ONLY in kaiser_normalize. An implementation that accepts a normalization switch and returns the same expectation for both values has a dead argument, whichever value it defaults to.
authority.does_not_claim: Which normalization is correct. Hendrickson & White 1964 take the orthogonal starting solution as given; Kaiser 1958 defines raw and normal varimax and recommends normal, but the Promax paper does not adopt that recommendation. Both ACCEPTABLE.

manifest.source_paper: Hendrickson & White 1964, Br. J. Stat. Psychol. 17(1):65-70; Kaiser 1958, Psychometrika 23(3):187-200
